blinding_guess.why: Ros_SimpleMsg_MotionReply (SimpleMessage.c:106-123) tests receiveMsg->header.msgType == ROS_MSG_MOTO_MOTION_CTRL twice; the second branch (line 112) is unreachable and was evidently meant for ROS_MSG_JOINT_TRAJ_PT_FULL. A reply to a JointTrajPtFull message therefore falls into the else branch and carries robot_id (groupNo) = -1, sequence = -1 and command = the message type (14), so MotoMotionReply.robot_id/.sequence never echo JointTrajPtFull.robot_id/.sequence even though the field comment says the sequence is echoed back.

notes: Scope: only the MotoPlus controller application under snapshot/fs100/MotoPlus (the ROS-side fs100 nodes under fs100/src and fs100/include, and dx100, are separate units and were not described). Transport is the ROS-Industrial simple_message binary protocol over raw TCP (motion server port TCP_PORT_MOTION 50240, state server TCP_PORT_STATE 50241); there are no ROS topics, so QoS is null (ROS 1 / not applicable) and no rate is set for these elements (the 25 ms STATE_UPDATE_MIN_PERIOD applies to JointFeedback/RobotStatus, not to the listed elements; replies are one per received message). Canonical names: the MotoPlus code never uses the packet's ROS type names; the types are C structs SmBodyMotoMotionReply, SmBodyMotoMotionCtrl and SmBodyJointTrajPtFull in SimpleMessage.h, identified on the wire by message type ids 2002, 2001 and 14. The packet field robot_id corresponds to the local member groupNo (first int, commented 'Robot/group ID; 0 = 1st robot') in both SmBodyMotoMotionReply and SmBodyJointTrajPtFull; declares entries use the packet's canonical element names in the template and record the local identifier in provenance. Field order of SmBodyMotoMotionReply is groupNo, sequence, command, result, subcode, data[10]; result is declared as the enum SmResultType. definition_id is null for every port: no .msg/.srv/.action/.idl definition exists for these simple_message types in the snapshot (they are C structs), ros_distro is null, and definition_hash.py does not apply to C headers. For that reason msg:motoman/MotoMotionReply, which this package does declare (SimpleMessage.h:189-197, type id ROS_MSG_MOTO_MOTION_REPLY = 2002, built in SimpleMessage.c:92-129 and sent at MotionServer.c:249), has no declares entry: the msg template requires a definition_id value that cannot be produced; it is deliberately not in not_declared. Frame: MotoMotionReply/MotoMotionCtrl fields are codes/ids (none); for JointTrajPtFull joint-space data no frame is declared (null); internally the increment moves use incData.frame = MP_INC_PULSE_DTYPE (MotionServer.c:829). Units for JointTrajPtFull come from struct comments; the code converts time to ms (MotionServer.c:1209 jointMotionData->time = (int)(jointTrajData->time * 1000);). The code also reads MotoMotionCtrl groupNo/sequence/command and JointTrajPtFull validFields/time/pos/vel/acc (local names); only packet elements are listed in references. Header comments give stale ids (// ROS_MSG_MOTO_MOTION_CTRL = 2011, // ROS_MSG_MOTO_MOTION_REPLY = 2012) while the enum values are 2001 and 2002. perm_requires records the REMOTE-mode check the code applies before accepting motion; it is an operating-mode precondition of the controller, not an access-control declaration.
